events.title: Oliver Pollock Creates the Dollar Sign Origin Record
events.description: New Orleans merchant Oliver Pollock, a financier of the American Revolution, used a handwritten symbol for the peso in a letter dated April 1, 1778, which is the earliest known instance of what became the dollar sign ($).
events.significance: The document marks the earliest known use of the symbol that became the dollar sign, one of the most recognized currency symbols in the world.

events.title: Adolf Hitler Sentenced to Prison for the Beer Hall Putsch
events.description: A Munich court sentenced Adolf Hitler to five years in Landsberg Prison for high treason after the failed 1923 Beer Hall Putsch. He served only about nine months, during which he dictated the first volume of Mein Kampf.
events.significance: The trial gave Hitler national publicity, and his early release allowed him to rebuild the Nazi Party and eventually seize power in 1933.

events.title: Battle of Okinawa Begins
events.description: Allied forces led by the United States landed on Okinawa on April 1, 1945, beginning the largest amphibious assault of the Pacific War and one of its bloodiest battles, which lasted until late June.
events.significance: The heavy casualties on both sides and among Okinawan civilians influenced Allied planning for an invasion of Japan and the decision to use atomic weapons.

events.title: Apple Computer Founded
events.description: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne founded Apple Computer on April 1, 1976, in Cupertino, California, to sell the Apple I personal computer built by Wozniak.
events.significance: Apple grew into one of the world's most valuable companies and shaped personal computing, digital music, smartphones, and consumer technology.

events.title: Netherlands Legalizes Same-Sex Marriage
events.description: The Netherlands became the first country in the world to give same-sex couples full legal marriage rights when its law took effect on April 1, 2001. Amsterdam's mayor married the first couples at midnight.
events.significance: The law set a precedent that many other countries later followed in recognizing marriage equality.
